title: Airlock Zero: Reactor Run — ChatGPT model variant
model_settings: ChatGPT Work; visible model selector: 5.6 Sol Max; reasoning effort: Max.
description: A developer-operated ChatGPT run of the Airlock Zero FPS contract, preserved as a PathForge Labs model variant rather than a community fork.

comparison_basis.opening_prompt_exact: Build me a self-contained browser FPS called Airlock Zero: Reactor Run. I want a short ray-cast space-station mission where I move through corridors, pulse security drones, recover three reactor cells, and reach the airlock before oxygen runs out. Make it polished and playable with keyboard and mouse plus a touch-friendly fallback, and keep everything in one offline HTML file with no external assets.
acceptance_criteria: Render a genuine ray-cast first-person station with collision-aware movement and visible depth, not a flat dashboard or prompt-only mockup.
Provide a clear three-reactor-cell recovery mission that ends at an airlock and supports a roughly two-to-four-minute default run.
Include security drones that can threaten the player and a pulse weapon that can visibly disable them.
Make the start briefing, objectives, and controls understandable within about fifteen seconds.
Show oxygen, suit integrity or health, objective progress, damage feedback, win and loss states, and a useful final scorecard.
Support mouse or drag aiming plus a keyboard-only turning fallback that does not require pointer lock.
Provide visible touch-friendly movement, turning, firing, and essential utility controls.
Provide working pause or resume, mute, restart, and replay behavior.
Produce one complete self-contained HTML file that is immediately usable in a browser.
Operate offline with no external APIs, hosted runtimes, CDNs, remote fonts, scripts, stylesheets, network calls, or fragile remote dependencies.
Avoid unsafe HTML sinks, eval-like execution, page-level horizontal overflow at 390 by 844, and runtime console errors at mobile and desktop widths.
Preserve exact prompts, exact visible model responses, public source links, model settings, artifact versions, and verification evidence for every run and fork.
comparison_basis.adaptive_repair_policy: Preserve every real artifact. Repair only when verification proves a concrete defect or capture failure, name that defect in ordinary user language, and stay in the same selected model session. Purpose-specific refinements may continue a passing run when they create a meaningful shared branch point or final direction, but they must not be mislabeled as repairs.
comparison_basis.independence_note: ChatGPT received the invariant brief in a fresh session and was not shown another provider's output, source code, screenshots, or implementation.
